cl_gen_drug_test_misses.q: Can a drug test miss fentanyl, or benzos like Xanax?
cl_gen_drug_test_misses.short: Yes. Expert reviews say standard opiate tests don't react to fentanyl at all. Most benzo tests can miss Xanax (alprazolam) unless the lab adds an extra step.
cl_gen_drug_test_misses.but: This is about urine tests, from expert reviews dated 2004 to 2017, not new studies. They give no numbers on how often a drug is missed, and tests change.
how: Quick urine tests, in a lab or on the spot, look only for what they're built to find. Most cover amphetamines, cocaine, cannabis, opiates and PCP, often benzos too. Cannabis tests don't catch synthetic cannabinoids, and tests for 'bath salts' haven't worked well.

Most opiate tests are set up for morphine. Fentanyl, methadone and buprenorphine don't react with them, and oxycodone only weakly. These need tests of their own, and some labs don't run them unless asked.

Most benzo tests can miss lorazepam and alprazolam (Xanax) unless the lab first treats the urine with an enzyme. Most labs don't. Clonazepam reacts poorly. In one study, quick tests never caught a single dose of flunitrazepam (Rohypnol), but lab methods did.

A negative only means the level was under the test's cutoff, or the test doesn't react to that drug. Lab tests like mass spectrometry find more. But they cost more and are mostly used to check positives. Many hospital labs can do little or none of it.
cl_gen_drug_test_misses.rate: Three expert reviews passing on other studies' findings, with no numbers on how often a drug is missed. The newest is from 2017, and tests change.

fentanyl-and-analogues.statement: If an opiate test is negative, there's no fentanyl.
fentanyl-and-analogues.why: Expert reviews say standard opiate tests are set up for morphine and don't react to fentanyl. Fentanyl needs a test of its own or a lab method.

benzodiazepines.statement: If a benzo test is negative, no benzos were taken.
benzodiazepines.why: Expert reviews say most benzo tests can miss Xanax and lorazepam unless the lab adds a step. A negative only means the level was under the cutoff.
